rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes cold spray deposition, whereas the paper used electrospark deposition (ESD) with electrodes consolidated by spark plasma sintering. These are fundamentally different coating/repair technologies.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions ambient to moderately elevated temperatures, inert atmosphere, and post-repair cyclic thermal/mechanical testing. The paper used SPS at high temperatures (850–1050 °C), ESD under Ar, and did not perform any aggressive service testing.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis relies on plastic deformation and solid-state bonding to avoid melting and hot cracking. The paper's mechanism involves pulsed spark melting, rapid solidification, and layer buildup, with defects arising from thermal stress and reduced ductility, not hot cracking avoidance.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced hot cracking and enhanced durability under aggressive service. The paper predicted improved coating continuity with more layers but increased oxidation and microfissuring, and did not test durability under aggressive conditions.
